messages:
maya: quick update — ran the lazy-prefix-eviction experiment against the prod-sim fleet this morning. observed ~18% improvement p95 for the chat model and ~9% token-cost reduction when measured over the 6h window. sharing numbers + rollout plan below.

kenji: awesome. what was the test workload and did you keep batching the same?

rachel: test workload = replay of last-week production traces (mixed seq lengths). batching unchanged. main change was eviction heuristic: we stop evicting short prefixes unless they haven't been used for prefix_len tokens. small config flip.

rachel: config we toggled:
```yaml
cache:
  policy: lazy_prefix_eviction
  prefix_len: 64
  ttl_ms: 3000
```

vince: numbers from the run: median latency ~3% better, p90 ~10%, p95 ~18%, p99 unchanged. token-cost-per-request dropped 9% after accounting for added KV hits. plotted on dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/bench/LP-2026-03

maya: validation: no quality regressions on our prompt set (evaluated 12k prompts). reruns with slightly longer prefixes (128) show diminishing returns.

kenji: any memory footprint change?

rachel: small uptick in KV memory (~4% peak) due to retaining more prefixes; still well under our safety threshold on dedicated hosts. we also added a background async eviction job to smooth peaks.

maya: rollout plan: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over next 48h if error/latency SLOs hold. will monitor model-level latency and cost dashboards, and auto-rollback trigger if p95 increases by >5% vs baseline.

deploy-bot: deploy started: release/lazy-prefix-eviction canary -> cluster-prod-sim (10% traffic) by @maya. CI checks passed.

vince: perf microbench harness and raw logs are in the bench repo (bench/experiments/lazy-prefix-2026-03). i pushed CSVs and the analysis notebook.

kenji: perfect. please add a note in the eng-runtime channel and include this in the next ops-runbook update. also can we tag the commit diff for audit?

maya: will do. tagging now and adding a short blurb to the weekly all-hands update. thanks team :tada:

rachel: follow-up: created a small feature flag for tuning prefix_len per-model. we can ramp per-model if one shows worse memory/cost tradeoffs.

kenji: love it. congrats on the win — big for cost ops.

maya: closing loop: if anyone sees anomalies ping me or drop in #eng-oncall.

vince: sending short email to cs and solutions with the cost-impact numbers.

deploy-bot: canary reached 50% at 1769001289. no rollback triggered.

maya: sweet — will start 50->100% after another sanity check at +6h.

kenji: :thumbsup:
